Skip wins when dispatch reaches the prompt: the dispatcher first settles those receipts durably, then drops it without a model turn and continues; settlement failure retains the skipped head instead of allowing replay ambiguity. The prompt stays visible with only its negative emoji, is excluded immediately from the executable queue count shared by the Pi status bar and Telegram main menu, and keeps a struck-through physical ordinal. Returning it to Keep restores its contribution to the count without moving it. Graceful session shutdown discards all remaining queue receipts before clearing session-local memory, and startup discards receipts only after proving their former process dead, so a new or unrelated session never inherits queued work. Queue item detail exposes horizontal Normal/Priority/Steer and Keep/Skip selectors instead of irreversible Delete. Legacy published Priority callbacks retain explicit lane intent. Dispatched/frozen items expose inspection only; an oversized idle Steer item stays editable with a Priority/Normal escape and never splits its source group.

Menu and reaction controls share the same canonical queue state. A menu Keep can clear internal Skip without changing Priority or queue position, but Telegram's Bot API cannot remove a reaction created by the user; the visible user reaction can therefore remain until that user removes it. Once a prompt is dispatched, frozen for an attempt, consumed or dropped, later reactions cannot change or reissue it. Steer freezes exact original objects before whole-receipt attempt disposition, which is not SDK/model-use proof. Active `turn_end` inserts one packet without resetting Telegram reply/preview ownership; packet content preserves original text/image blocks with blank-line separators only between prompts, without numbered Steer labels. Idle origin detection retains its Telegram prefix. Idle `sendUserMessage` pins the first original and its tail until `agent_start` projects one reply/voice/attachment owner. Partial/refused/unknown outcomes remain protected without replay, and Steer queue transfer requires independently negotiated `queue-steer-v1` plus base handoff support at every participant before custody changes. Frozen/pending work never transfers as unspent input; missing support or malformed attempted/projection fields fail closed.

Guest Mode is the deliberate exception to deferred Keep/Skip semantics. A guest prompt has no source message reaction surface and may share zero-valued chat/message placeholders with other guest prompts, so queue-menu callbacks address it by immutable `queueOrder` and expose an immediate `Skip`. The leader settles its durable admission, removes it while other agent work may continue, stops placeholder animation, and replaces the inline globe placeholder with non-printing content. Bot API inline messages have no delete method, so this visual clear is the supported deletion equivalent. A successfully skipped waiting guest prompt never reaches a model turn. Once dispatched, its retained head is inspection-only until `agent_start` consumes that exact reply owner; stale Guest Skip callbacks refuse without receipt disposal or placeholder dismissal. Later waiting guests remain independently skippable.

A standalone `/continue` is a source-addressed control-lane prompt, not a Normal/Priority prompt. An authorized thumbs-down reaction to its original chat/message immediately settles the exact waiting continuation's receipts before removing it, even while unrelated work is active. Failed or unknown settlement retains it for the existing reaction retry path; duplicate reactions cannot settle twice. Positive reactions and removal of the negative reaction neither change its control lane nor reconstruct cancelled work. The dispatched head awaiting `agent_start` and already-started work are never cancelled; appends and reorders preserve that Pi-owned head. Synthetic model-switch continuations have no source message IDs and are not reaction-addressable by their fallback reply anchor. Reaction authorization and chat/message namespace isolation remain unchanged.

Admission and planning validate lane contracts. Invalid lane/kind pairings fail predictably instead of being silently coerced.

Prompt preparation completes downloads, inbound handlers, and binary image reads before synchronous final assembly and queue commit. Enqueue captures only intended abort-history identities before preparation; afterward it reads the current queue, folds surviving selected prompts using their current text and receipts, allocates the new turn's order, and appends without another asynchronous boundary. The handed-off head remains in place until `agent_start` consumes it, even if preparation finishes first. Concurrent arrivals, removals, and lane/reaction edits remain intact; preparation failure or stale-generation completion leaves intervening queue changes untouched.

Dispatch requires:

- No active Telegram turn.
- No pending Telegram dispatch already sent to Pi.
- No compaction in progress.
- `ctx.isIdle()` is true.
- `ctx.hasPendingMessages()` is false.

A dispatched prompt remains queued until `agent_start` consumes it. This keeps the active Telegram turn bound for previews, attachments, aborts, and final replies. A low-level `agent_end` error also retains that active turn because Pi may retry automatically; a later successful `agent_end` delivers through the original target and metadata, while `agent_settled` proves that an unrecovered error can be finalized once before queue dispatch resumes.

Post-agent-end queue dispatch uses a session-bound deferred dispatcher. It is activated on session start, clears timers on shutdown, and skips callbacks from older generations before touching `ExtensionContext`. Dispatch stays session-bound after polling ownership moves elsewhere. When a queued Telegram prompt is forwarded into Pi, the bridge synchronously commits its exact durable receipt before calling normal `sendUserMessage(content)`; failed receipt commitment blocks dispatch, while the unavoidable crash window between commitment and Pi admission favors at-most-once execution over replay. It does not use Pi's `followUp` delivery option or inject terminal input.

Settlement returns an explicit acknowledgement only after exact source removal is confirmed. Missing readiness, frozen/transferred ownership, observation failure and an unknown completion result are not acknowledgements. The mux resolves every unsettled receipt to its owning runtime before mutation, rejects unknown/conflicting ownership, and requires each completion result; a completed prefix is not whole-request success. A private weak acknowledgement keyed by the original receipt object and its unchanged normalized metadata lets later local discard clean up a confirmed prompt still awaiting `agent_start`, including after worker replacement. It is never execution authority: it neither re-arms dispatch nor survives cloning/serialization, and is not a durable completion ledger. Failed or ambiguous completion creates no acknowledgement: prompt dispatch and bulk clearing retain the local item rather than inferring success from an absent source. This does not establish retention for every internal mutation primitive: direct message-ID removal still updates memory before containing settlement failure. Its former automatic Business-deletion producer was invalid because Business and bot-chat namespaces are independent, and default routing now ignores it. Do not restore that producer or infer private-message deletion intent from matching numeric IDs. The internal explicit deletion plan and helper are not a new automatic deletion capability.

One monotonic session generation also fences agent/tool/message events, compaction callbacks, preview state, scheduled final delivery, controls, and shutdown. Distinct Pi context objects observed within one session adopt that generation; contexts already observed under an older generation remain stale after replacement. Session start invalidates pending preview work, delayed finals check their captured context before delivery, and shutdown rechecks after asynchronous polling/preview boundaries with a bounded preview-clear wait.

For a configured Rich response with final text and exactly one supported queued PNG/JPEG, MP4, or MP3 artifact, queue orchestration asks `outbound-attachments` for one reply-anchored multipart Rich result before finalizing ordinary text. A successful result clears the preview, records exact message ownership, and suppresses duplicate text/file delivery. A known-safe rejection returns to the established paths; an ambiguous send stops the turn without fallback or replay. HTML mode, multiple or unsupported files, Guest Mode, and all voice-policy outputs bypass this optimization.

#### Queue Lifetime

The prompt queue is session-local, not a restart-persistent inbox. Waiting prompts are discarded on shutdown and dead-owner cleanup, and dispatch stays connected-local as described above. The operator excluded restart-persistent prompt storage from 0.52.0 and future plans to avoid unnecessary complexity; it is cancelled, not deferred. Operator rule before any reload or restart: wait for the queue to drain, or knowingly accept losing the waiting work and re-send what still matters afterwards. Nothing is preserved or replayed automatically. Existing durable admission, receipt ownership, custody and anti-replay protections remain unchanged and do not promise reconstruction of the waiting prompt queue.

### Controls And Menus

Telegram controls execute through command/callback domains, not by entering the normal prompt queue unless they intentionally create a prompt turn. Built-in read-only menu commands are admitted once required local state mutation finishes: first-user pairing still persists before `/start` is accepted, while menu rendering and BotFather command synchronization run as context-fenced best-effort effects with diagnostic failure sinks. Their unresolved Telegram calls therefore cannot retain the durable polling offset or prevent the next `getUpdates` request. Detached effects, deferred dispatch/watchdog, typing, and diagnostics callbacks contain primary and diagnostic failure; stale typing context is ignored, while snapshot publication serializes one write plus one retained coalesced rerun. Raw companion handlers still run before durable built-in routing and should return quickly even though their execution no longer retains polling.

Immediate controls:

- `/start` opens the main inline application menu.
- `/model`, `/thinking`, `/queue`, and `/settings` are hidden shortcuts to menu sections.
- `/compact` opens an inline confirmation dialog and then runs compaction when the bridge is idle.
- `/next` dispatches the next queued turn, aborting Pi first when needed. Target-bound command composition must forward the announcement request, exact-turn marker, superseding cancellation, and deferred-dispatch ports rather than silently dropping them. Active-turn settlement attempts its abort notice against the interrupted prompt before queue dispatch continues; definite or ambiguous notice failure is recorded but cannot block the selected turn. The queue owner then emits `Dispatching next queued turn.` against the exact selected prompt's chat/thread/reply id before its one model dispatch; skipped, inactive, pending-mutation, and admission-blocked candidates never receive it. A successful dispatch notice carries its reply-dedup anchor through the following agent-start reset, so later messages in that turn do not repeat the queued-prompt reply header. A later `/abort` or `/stop` cancels both pending `/next` notices before taking ownership, preventing duplicate abort results and stale future dispatch announcements. The `/next` command itself is never a lifecycle-notice reply target. Aborted pending assistant text is not projected as a second reply, while already completed intermediate output remains visible.
- `/abort` aborts active work while preserving queued items. Abort-history preservation is enabled only for Telegram-owned active turns; later local/non-Telegram agent starts clear stale abort-history mode so the next Telegram prompt appends instead of absorbing old queued turns as history.
- `/stop` aborts and clears waiting Telegram queue items.

Queued controls:

- `/continue` creates a Telegram-owned `continue` prompt in the highest-priority control lane. A negative reaction to the original standalone command cancels it only while waiting, with exact durable settlement as specified above.
- Prompt-template commands expand Telegram-safe Pi template aliases before entering the prompt queue.
- Model-switch continuation uses the control lane when any interruptible in-flight agent run in the current Pi session must be stopped and resumed. A Telegram-owned run retains its prompt target; otherwise the exact model-menu chat/Thread/message supplies continuation and reply ownership.

Queue and menu mutations are reachable through Telegram updates handled by the current polling owner. After ownership moves, the old instance keeps processing its accepted local queue, but it no longer receives new menu callbacks or control updates for remote mutation. UI label, navigation, tab, toggle, card, and dialog rules are defined in [UI Style](./ui-style.md). Callback prefix ownership is defined in [Callback Namespaces](./callback-namespaces.md).

### Confirmation Requests (Planned)

**Unreleased implementation; integrated review and release acceptance remain open.** The existing `delivery` domain provides the producer-requested binary-confirmation request/decision mechanism. Ordinary/selected `/new` and `/compact`, plus hidden `/quit`, use it. Settings cleanup and routing cancellation retain their native work-set/source protocols under the [local producer assessment](#native-confirmation-producer-assessment-local). Confirmation is a higher-level interaction over an operational view, not a separate domain or independently bound runtime: reuse Delivery's target resolution, generation, logical-view ownership and operation ordering, adding only the pending-answer substate. The public membrane remains `/delivery`; command and destructive-operation execution owners remain separate. The public request/handle/result shape is owned by [Confirm API](./public-api.md#confirm-api-unreleased), not a separate design document. The `/delivery` export, shared-runtime race tests and authorized callback routing establish local implementation, not released or live-session availability.

Within Delivery, Confirm and Choice share one pending-question pool, operation queue and terminal transition mechanism. Public Choice has its own explicit request/result function, immutable option snapshot and reserved `tgchoice:` controls; it never accepts the private native-command mapping supplied to Confirm. Disabled or wrong-kind controls cannot consume a question. The shared capability owns dialog rendering, correlation and one-shot answer mechanics. Each request captures an immutable owner, runtime/session generation, profile, exact chat/Thread, published message and fresh random nonce. The allowed operator, current binding and callback eligibility are checked before acceptance. Session replacement or loss of authorized binding invalidates the request; old dialogs never retarget. Callback data contains only a short opaque identifier and choice within Telegram's byte limit. Producers retain the semantic action/target snapshot, approval policy, execution authorization and post-wait validity checks. This is opt-in reuse of bridge mechanics, never generic mirroring or resolution of foreign UI dialogs.

The first eligible answer atomically settles the request before asynchronous UI cleanup. Repeated clicks cannot produce another decision. The lifetime starts at request admission, including delivery wait. Abort/expiry before publication forbids further sends; already-issued transport cannot be retroactively unsent. An unknown send outcome revokes the nonce without automatic replay, so a possibly remaining message is inert. Failed deletion/editing of a settled dialog cannot alter the decision or repeat an operation. Pending state belongs to the live runtime and is not revived after reload; this is not a durable workflow engine or an exactly-once business-effect guarantee.

Opening must return without waiting for a human, and an original serialized Telegram update handler must not await the decision promise. A built-in adapter consumes accepted decisions within the existing callback execution path rather than replacing source custody or capturing a stale Pi command context:

- `/new` retains callback admission, acknowledgement/confirmation cleanup, completion and removal of the exact durable update, then dispatch through the runtime-armed typed Pi gateway. Its pending continuation captures semantic session generation, profile/operator and the original source journal namespace; a foreign completion with the same numeric update ID cannot release it, and late owner loss cannot invoke `newSession`. Namespace correlation uses the existing worker-bound admission carrier, not deferred-input evidence or a completion grant. Session replacement never starts from an ordinary decision-promise continuation or while inbound authority is unsettled. Existing discriminated handoff, successor claim and exact leader/follower ownership remain authoritative.
- Hidden `/quit` uses the same one-shot dialog and exact source-journal completion barrier, but does not publish replacement handoff or enqueue the `/new` gateway. Public `ExtensionContext.abort()` / `shutdown()` work outside command contexts, so the completion continuation resolves the fresh current SDK context directly; waiting for a command/model turn could defeat busy-instance rescue. Semantic session/profile/operator authority is checked before dispatch and again after cancellation. A local quitting flag fences normal and Steer dispatch from confirmed scheduling, including completion-observer dispatch before abort. It does not discard work early; the unchanged normal session-shutdown policy later disposes remaining queue authority before clearing memory. Abort errors remain diagnostic and do not prevent a still-authorized shutdown attempt; shutdown is single-attempt with no force-kill fallback or durable restart intent. Normal Pi shutdown hooks own resource release and configured Thread cleanup. Feedback says requested, never proves the process has exited.
- `/compact` retains a fresh idle/queue check after confirmation. Compaction startup, completion/error handling, queue release and owned typing stay with the compaction domain.
- Settings cleanup and routing cancellation are not additional Delivery decision waiters. Settings keeps exact reviewed work-set identity, Back navigation, fresh protection, Workspace deletion permits and commit-only recovery; Routing keeps original-source custody and its explicit action/recovery controls. A shared dialog answer cannot substitute for either protocol.

Native command questions retain their original bold question, button order and callback feedback, expire after five minutes, and refuse old unbound `new:confirm|cancel` / `compact:confirm|cancel` controls. The private producer port supplies captured publication and command mapping separately from the public request; a producer name or extra request fields cannot grant native command authority. Native question publication and accepted feedback opt explicitly into caller-local UI issuance/ACK fences, carried through rendered send/edit overflow and callback acknowledgement. Direct transport promotes them to native API admission checks; followers keep callable checks in local IPC options while leader registration/target/message-ownership validation remains separate. Full transport authority still refuses follower serialization; no command/execution grant is weakened. Captured recipient/dialog/source predicates remain checked before and after API waits, then the existing producer takes over business execution and durable-source completion. Transport/view replacement does not by itself revoke an already admitted semantic session action. Remaining integrated review and release gates are tracked in [BACKLOG.md](../BACKLOG.md#declarative-interaction-apis-minor-release).

The next minor release includes the [declarative interaction APIs](./public-api.md#planned-declarative-interaction-apis): Choice, Artifact Delivery and Task View have local unreleased implementations; Text Input and Attachment Request remain planned separate functions, not a public dialog factory. Reuse pending-answer/view lifecycle within Delivery where it fits; routing and inbound/media owners retain exact source classification, download and disposition. Text/attachment replies need proven association to the requesting extension before agent admission, including explicit ambiguity, late/reload and media-group rules. Outgoing artifacts reuse existing file transport/validation. Task View owns only progress projection and cancellation requests; producers own task execution, semantic validation and completion. The unimplemented functions remain planned boundaries, not permission to create a parallel registry, capture every next message, mirror foreign UI or expose raw Pi contexts. SDK question send/edit and generic callback acknowledgement distinguish full native API authority from explicitly local UI issuance/ACK checks. Direct transport promotes those local checks to native admission guards; followers keep them only in caller-owned IPC options, with plain single-attempt policy on the wire. Local checks never become leader authority: authenticated registration, generation and target checks stay leader-owned, and full transport callbacks still refuse follower serialization.

#### Native Confirmation Producer Assessment (Local)

The current built-in producer inventory is an ownership assessment, not independent integrated review or live acceptance. It selects no further migration merely to make every human action a binary question:

- **Command questions — shared Delivery:** `commands.sendTelegramConfirmation()` publishes `/new`, `/compact` and hidden `/quit` through the existing confirmation port; Routing dispatches only their accepted native mappings. Delivery owns one-shot answers, while Commands/Runtime retain the semantic action and exact source-completion barriers. Ordinary and selected command paths keep their existing recipient guards; no generic command-name execution grant is added.
- **Settings inactive-tab cleanup — retained domain review:** `menu-settings` renders the reviewed count, deletion consequences, Back and `settings:clean:<operationId>`. Root composes `thread-cleanup-manager.review/clean`, not a Delivery answer continuation. The canonical work-set and manual deletion fence retain exact candidates, fresh authority/protection and sole permits. Repeating Clean may finish a known commit-ready outcome without another delete; an unknown deletion stays protected. A spent ephemeral Confirm nonce cannot replace that recovery identity, and an additional Yes/No would duplicate the existing explicit Clean action. Keep the current review/navigation controls and fenced coordinator.
- **Per-input routing Cancel — source action, not another question:** `routing.handleUnboundRerouteCancelCallback()` requires the original untouched chooser, human owner, source/execution fences and profile admission before committed private cancellation. Chooser retirement and conditional tab cleanup follow that outcome; sibling custody remains independent. The adopted routing UX requires no extra confirmation. A Delivery decision must neither settle those sources nor supply created-tab/orphan deletion authority.
- **Pending cancellation recovery — source-owned review:** `routing.handleCancellationReview()` binds a current review/message to exact native retained originals, supports refresh/pagination and retries only the selected source's original disposition capability under fresh profile admission. A view-update failure may leave cancellation committed and its original recovery result useful. Keep that status/retry protocol instead of replacing it with one-shot Yes/No state or reopening input as a new question.
- **Connection takeover/disconnect — Pi UI:** the two `ctx.ui.confirm` producers in `commands` belong to the operator's local connection commands. Their currentness checks and transport/session consequences remain producer-owned. Do not automatically mirror or resolve them through Telegram Delivery. Planned pairing, agent `tgbtn` collectors and private Text/Attachment work remain separate scopes, not missing native-confirmation adapters.

This boundary follows the existing Settings review/Back, exact slotless-target, changed/protected candidate, lost-ACK commit-only recovery, pending-cancellation review and unavailable-view custody regressions in `tests/menu-settings.test.ts`, `tests/thread-cleanup-manager.test.ts` and `tests/routing.test.ts`. The composed full-suite result supplies local regression evidence, not an independent reviewer or a live deletion grant. A future explicitly selected UX adaptation would need its own original producer/physical transition and preservation witnesses; this assessment adds no callback registry, durable workflow, waiter or execution authority.

### Attachment Request Preparation (Planned, Unwired)

**Current-tree boundary:** retained private question/publication/privacy kernels are not an accepting Attachment collector. Removed source-ingress, capture/seal, consumer-lease and warm-disposition assemblies and their end-to-end checkpoints are held on `wip/private-input-foundations`; older checkpoint descriptions below are not current callable source owners or re-landing/readiness evidence. See the [public boundary](./public-api.md#attachment-request-boundary-planned).

> **Release scope:** the private Attachment Request capture, file seal, lease accounting, staging and warm disposition code described in this section is not part of the current tree. The unreleased implementation, tests and the design records cut from here are preserved on local branch `wip/private-input-foundations`; remaining text records boundaries that still apply to the shipped code. See the re-landing item in [BACKLOG.md](../BACKLOG.md).

**Private question/receiver observation, metadata preflight and native held capture are implemented here; no public Attachment opener, file collector, peer capability or production readiness is available.** The [frozen authoring limits](./public-api.md#element-specific-fields) remain unchanged. Reuse Delivery for question publication, receiver identity, deadline/abort, pending capacity and typed one-shot settlement; Updates/Routing retain early sender-authorized interception and exact source disposition; Media owns bounded attachment interpretation; API owns actual download/streaming and scratch files. Producers retain semantic validation, file-use authorization, execution and disposal. Add no interactions domain, global registry, poller, persistent root or generic workflow engine.

#### Existing Owners Are Not Private Admission

`collectTelegramFileInfos()` is an ordinary prompt helper: it walks Rich Message blocks, selects photo renditions and globally deduplicates by file ID. Two physical source messages with different request reply anchors can therefore become one file-info row. Count and correlate physical message/media occurrences before that projection; matching file IDs are not proof of a shared receiver or source disposition. Photo renditions are one attachment, not separate response files. Any legitimate native alias needs explicit interpretation, not a blanket permission to deduplicate ambiguous payloads. Sender MIME/name metadata is untrusted; MIME filters do not validate content and filename extensions are not filters.

`createTelegramMediaGroupController()` and `transitionTelegramPendingGroups()` serialize bounded debounce batches, including later members of the same album in another dispatch. A quiet timer or closed worker batch does not certify Telegram album completeness. Do not accept a prefix or silently drop unsupported members. Whole-source membership and one exact receiver must be established before atomic request acceptance; otherwise use the private refusal/held disposition, never ordinary model/STT/handler fallback. This is not permission to capture unrelated next messages while a request waits.

`downloadTelegramMessageFiles()` sequentially invokes a path-returning port and does not own rollback of earlier successful files. The current Bridge download port supplies its configured per-file cap, not a request-wide remaining budget or receiver lifetime. Low-level `downloadTelegramFile()` already checks metadata/header hints and actual streamed bytes, supports an AbortSignal and cleans its own failed `.part`; it publishes to a deterministic scoped name, not a unique request lease. Reuse those mechanisms through a reviewed private capture port, not by exposing raw client/options or broadening generic IPC/file-read authority. Two native four-byte downloads can both pass a four-byte per-file limit while exceeding a six-byte response budget. Metadata size is only a preflight refusal hint; success needs bounded actual sizes summed across the entire response.

`cleanupTelegramTempFiles()` is an age-only regular-file janitor; it has no source-pin or consumer-lease contract. Scratch age cannot authorize deletion of held private input. Existing ordinary media behavior remains unchanged: these are integration gaps, not new guarantees silently assigned to legacy helpers.

#### Required Capture And Lifetime Boundary

Before any private getFile/content I/O, retain the exact live request, original publication, configured operator/bot/profile/session/chat/Thread, source membership and actual receiver/transport authority. Count/filter/shape failure leaves the question waiting under its original deadline and privately refuses the input without a partial result. Recheck around asynchronous boundaries and before handing any path/metadata to the original producer. Cancellation ends collection, never invokes Pi abort, transcribes audio, reroutes to a replacement receiver or grants business execution. An unknown download/submission/disposition outcome requires owner-specific reconciliation, not blind recapture or an ordinary prompt copy.

One request-owned operation reserves the whole response budget. Lower configured limits win; each stream is bounded by the remaining total, with safe actual-byte accounting and no successful subset. Capture into uniquely owned scratch artifacts under the existing temp owner; failure/expiry/abort rolls back only those artifacts after actual I/O settles. Logical cancellation cannot release actual-work reservations or delete an in-flight writer prematurely. Preserve generation/source/operation identity and do not remove pre-existing or another request's deterministic cache path.

Keep admission-owned files pinned while any exact source disposition remains held or uncertain. A positively delivered producer result carries explicit `expiresAt` and the existing ten-minute default consumer lease, clipped by runtime policy; consumers copy what they need longer. Consumer expiry/disposal alone cannot clear a still-held source pin, and pin release alone cannot delete an unexpired consumer lease. Generic scratch cleanup must not sweep these files; no secure-erasure, kernel-cancellation, global filesystem atomicity or exactly-once business-effect claim is made.

#### Private Attachment Question/Receiver (Implemented, Unwired)

Delivery's private `openAttachmentQuestion()` shares the existing 256-interaction pool, per-target actual queue, deadline/abort and one-shot retirement with Confirm/Choice/Text/Task. It is not `openTelegramAttachmentRequest` and grants no source admission, file I/O or business execution. Its native handle/result reports cancellation, expiry, abort or invalidation; the separate private SDK boundary below can now additionally settle a structured submitted-files result, without an accepting source collector or production composition. It snapshots bounded owner/question/cancel copy, scope and signal; private MIME/count/total limits match the frozen defaults and reuse Media's immutable constraint normalizer. Limits remain metadata, not validation of uploaded content or actual bytes.

The kernel requires both an explicit complete-path `getAttachmentReceiverBotId` and dedicated `publishAttachmentQuestion` port. Production composition/Lifecycle leave both unbound. The Bridge supports private direct and scoped follower opt-ins below. The broker has separate authenticated opt-in support; neither is production readiness. The original-publication owner must supply the dedicated path; ordinary sendChunk cannot substitute for it. A positive native message ID creates a waiting question; opening and unknown-send attempts create no usable receiver and no guessed cleanup. Native publisher/authority/target/readiness callables retain their original identities. Readiness cannot mutate an authority object to retarget publication. UI uses a bold escaped question, an explicit reply-to-this-message instruction and the original cancel control, not a native file-picker promise.

`captureAttachmentReceiver()` observes only an exact waiting native question: nonce, physical published message, operator/profile/bot/chat/Thread and original native ports. The frozen guard snapshots identity and exposes `assertCurrent`; Attachment additionally carries the fixed intake limits/deadline below. It neither settles/reserves an answer, installs/disposes timers/listeners nor mutates UI/Queue. Observed failure permanently ends that retained guard. Text and Attachment receivers share the non-settling mechanism, not identities or journal latches; a physical publication ambiguous across the two kinds refuses both. Private `captureTelegramAttachmentReceiver()` adds the existing registration membrane, shared with Text: it freezes the caller snapshot without creating a missing registry, captures the exact global registry/runtime/binding/capture callable and retains the returned guard callable. Binding/provider loss during capture or assertion refuses/ends that guard; same-object, same-generation and equal-value restoration cannot repair observed history. Absent/older Attachment receivers never fall back to Text or an accepting collector. This is non-settling receiver observation, not whole-source custody or original-publication adapter readiness.

`tgattach:<nonce>:cancel` is reserved before ordinary callback/model routing, including malformed, stale or unbound controls. Exact current cancellation settles only the private question and retains a status marker; it never aborts Pi, disposes consumer file leases or releases source pins. Callback namespace reservation does not recognize/admit attachment message bodies. The direct original-publication adapter is privately implemented below; early reply provenance/privacy, genuine whole-source disposition, complete peer intake compatibility and positive producer handoff remain unimplemented. The tests exercise real kernel/Router code under trusted native test ports, not executed production publication or live Telegram clients.

#### Attachment Native SDK Result (Implemented, Unwired)

A native question reservation now optionally exposes a synchronous `handoff(materialize)` capability. This is an SDK-local boundary over the original pending producer's actual native result promise, not source admission, a public opener or IPC. The existing question record consumes the one handoff and takes custody of that exact native file provider before observing authority or invoking it. It does not introduce another registry/mailbox/executor. Competing/repeated attempts, caught reentry and decline after handoff cannot reopen the slot.

The provider first receives a frozen SDK custody scope. Its current `assertAcknowledged()` witnesses native SDK ownership of the provider while the original question/reservation remains valid; it is not producer result delivery or source completion. Native assembly can use this read-only witness for the capture kernel's lease attestor after `beginHandoff`, without invoking delivery/business execution from that attestor. Real positive identity followed by failure is only diagnostic `observedReceipt`. Artifact-only observer handling retains the original native error and ordered secondary recovery/diagnostic causes in a private carrier; rejection classification unwraps only that trusted carrier, not arbitrary cause metadata. Positive direct HTTP issuance is monotonic; legitimate follower pre-IPC no-issuance proof remains distinct. Across JSON retain safe category/issuance/correlation, not object identity or raw secret/path/body text. No absence-as-completion/submission or business grant.

Locks captures the current owned transport lifetime without lending the exact polling-startup context to Delivery. It retains that context internally and fences polling generation, leader epoch, session and ownership, with sticky observed invalidation across suspension/restart/conflict/loss. Same-session fresh caller contexts are not transport replacement. The context-bound `captureTransportAuthority(ctx)` API is unchanged. BusApi lazily combines this actual owner capture with Queue's profile/token generation stamp; a separately observed change/restoration cannot renew the operation. Lifecycle owns the captured session generation/ID guard. The composition root assembles these ports without local capture policy or eager access to the later-created Locks runtime.

Artifact incarnation metadata is excluded from legacy Restore hint comparison, consistently with the bus observation owner. This compatibility normalization leaves registration generation, session, target, protocol and currentness checks intact and does not relax Artifact wire authority.

Local mirrored/public/integration acceptance covers exact bytes/name/target, descriptor capture and late cleanup, bounded ledger nonretention, dedup/collision/incarnation/cache behavior, mixed direct/follower contention, original-operation IPC/HTTP outcomes and observer failures. Generated-package public-consumer fixtures load the compiled owners through actual package export resolution with no implementation-source fallback. The full native suite also passes. These are mocked-HTTP/local-IPC fixtures, not the entire compiled Pi production-root lifecycle, all supported-platform filesystem/socket behavior or live Bot API acceptance. Supported-platform and live acceptance remain gated in the canonical backlog; no entire compiled Pi lifecycle guarantee follows. Source implementation and current `dist` do not imply activation in the running session.

### Composable Interaction Surfaces (Planned)

**Agent Confirm/Choice markup is implemented locally; broader text/file surfaces and live/release acceptance remain open.** The agent and companion SDK planes are distinct. The SDK batch/waiter contract does not govern agent selection: a completed answer creates ordinary user input, while multiselect intermediate clicks change only finite local UI state. Shared JSON/CML validation is not a requirement to use SDK collectors, native answer Promises or new model tools.

#### Agent Composition And Results

- **Markup:** Interleave Markdown with `telegram_confirm` / `telegram_choice` JSON fences or HTML comments. Choice matrices retain horizontal rows and disabled cells. The exact schema and supported envelopes live in [public-api.md](./public-api.md#agent-selection-markup).
- **Interaction:** Each supported single-question button is an existing `tgbtn` action capturing only question and visible answer label for ordinary model input. No tags, version, kind, status or ID are forwarded. Bridge-local routing class prevents slash/app-like data from invoking methods. String choices and bare-string Confirm simplify authoring; richer SDK results stay separate.
- **Feedback:** Buttons begin neutral even when a style is declared. The declared style selects post-click feedback only. New selection controls use footer keyboards in both rendering modes so the existing keyboard edit can show selection. Legacy in-body button behavior is unchanged.
- **Admission:** The ordinary sender-authorized callback/routing/Queue path remains authoritative. Consume before callbacks, retain exact current target/reply context and preserve existing duplicate/failed-admission policy. No fake tool/system messages, private SDK-to-agent forwarding, hidden waiting model call or inspection tool.
- **Collection direction (explicitly authorized):** A Choice object is one question; a question array is a sequential wizard. `select:N` requires exactly N enabled choices, with toggles/progress but no intermediate model prompt. Complete results are a plain question/answer object or ordered array, with multi-answers as label arrays. Exact-N collection is implemented locally: neutral buttons toggle checkmarks/pressed colors, the cancel control shows selected/required counts, and completion produces one label array. Question arrays are sequential wizards: retain one current step and collected immutable answer data, advance locally, then emit one ordered array at completion. A one-question array keeps aggregate shape. Cancel emits completed answers plus the current question/cancel label, never an uncompleted set or unseen question. Independent blocks remain independent. Skill recipes decide usage; no arbitrary branching workflow or mirrored SDK protocol is introduced.
- **Bounds:** Validate a whole declaration before registering any of its cells. At most 16 recognized declarations and 64 selection cells activate per final answer; overflow creates no selection controls. Invalid blocks are bounded noninteractive diagnostics; incomplete fences publish nothing. Drafts suppress declaration bodies. Wizard projection bounds the whole composed view for every future question to one editable message before real callback registration. Unknown outcomes never spill into extra messages or retry. Existing button/comment literal and delimiter rules remain intact.
- **Lifetime:** The existing button store enforces original deadlines, consumes attempts before callbacks and retires superseded collector keys. A scalar question has one completion group; selecting either branch removes all siblings synchronously. Terminal collectors remove remaining group entries before external transport/admission callbacks; unknown edits or owner loss purge the shared collector associations. Queue/display errors cannot reopen spent work. Completion metadata stays bridge-local, never in model input. Completed scalar controls are remembered in the response-local footer so a subsequent collector rebuild cannot republish their old callback IDs. A response-local footer revision serializes collector edits and refreshes all active groups, preserving independent controls without stale overwrite; one unref nearest-deadline timer owns memory expiry, without a persistent registry or polling loop. Capture the production session/profile/bot/operator, role/epoch or follower generation/target at initial registration. Loss is sticky across revisions and awaited edits. Local-only API guards cross no IPC as functions or execution grants. Missing ports, malformed/cross-message callbacks and unknown edits refuse; unknown UI outcomes close the shared collector footer. Only a positive guarded edit ACK permits final ordinary queue admission; an admission error cannot replay it. Wizard deadlines use the earliest declared timeout from original planning, never per-step renewal. Opaque compiler fragments materialize only the active heading in the cached delivery text; decoded data is never rescanned as markup. Variable row spans rebuild under the shared footer revision. Replies owns the bounded single-message Rich/HTML editor; Routing joins its original execution/selection guards to native UI authority. Production edits use existing guarded `editMessageText`, with rich content retained rather than downgraded or re-chunked.

#### Independent Menu And Callback Retention

System menu state is a separate session-local store: at most 60 saved menu messages across Status, Model, Thinking, Queue and Settings, with a sliding one-hour idle lifetime refreshed on lookup. Lazy store/read pruning expires idle entries and evicts the oldest access-ordered entries; it does not automatically edit old keyboards. Core menu access neither consumes nor renews `tgbtn` entries.

Plain/app-bound prompt callbacks default to a fixed 24-hour lifetime, restoring the ordinary-button baseline rather than applying a question's one-hour default to every prompt. Production Confirm/Choice planners now default to 24 hours; raw compiler embedding that omits the private policy retains its one-hour compatibility default; explicit shorter deadlines still win and wizard progression never renews its original deadline. SDK Delivery timeout/capacity and private Text/Attachment defaults are unchanged. The separate callback store admits at most 60 retained associations. Each ordinary/app-bound action counts once; scalar question branches share a completion group and related collectors share a footer retirement owner. Capacity evicts the oldest complete group using its original creation age, not its newest callback generation. Drop every record before retirement hooks; retired identities cannot be reused. Registration reserves a slot before authority callbacks and rejects caught reentry without poisoning independent work. New app views remove superseded bound callback records and stale same-generation revisions cannot replace newer records. A no-effect compilation pass counts every callback kind and the sum of widest future wizard steps before real registration, rejecting a whole oversized publication rather than leaving partial controls. Disabled cells cost zero and future callback IDs are not retained. Timed memory expiry runs even with no further input. A single unref timer is re-armed to the earliest retained deadline, cancelled when empty/cleared and protected against stale timer generations. Exact legacy expiry is inclusive at its deadline; collector revisions retain their original declaration deadline. Retirement-hook/diagnostic failures cannot interrupt other cleanup. Lifecycle binding clears associations before session-start/shutdown awaits, but a stale shutdown never clears successor work. Actual in-flight edits remain awaited and their retired collector guards refuse late admission. Native Generative App owner observations now revoke stale app-bound callbacks without requiring a replacement view, including agent-only invocations. The native result fence and actual-execution ordering are specified in [Generative Apps lifecycle](./generative-apps.md#lifecycle-and-safety); independent live/platform/package acceptance remains separate.

The Bus-aware API observes local send/edit attempts and positive acknowledgements through a narrow store-owned port; no functions or new authority facts cross IPC. First acknowledged numeric chat/message coordinates pin each callback; copied messages cannot retarget it. Supplied send Thread coordinates, including an explicitly absent Thread, are preserved rather than inferred from a configured default. Bot API edits identify a message by chat/message ID and may lack a Thread field; such an edit pins only its known coordinates, without inventing a Thread. A production callback without acknowledged publication is unavailable. Capture original session/transport/operator/role authority for ordinary callbacks as well as collectors; spend scalar groups before even invoking captured authority observations.

The same store owns at most sixty indexed publication snapshots and a single coalescing footer-cleanup shell, not another interaction registry. Actual native sends/edits retain their attempts until settlement. A known publication serializes its native mutations, including cleanup, through a bounded sixty-attempt lane; cleanup cannot race an earlier edit or overwrite a later one. Consumption/closure marks spent `tgbtn` cells disabled. Known deadline retirement best-effort marks the label `Expired:` and replaces its executable ID with non-action `tgbtn:expired`; a delivered tap receives `Button action expired`. Capacity retirement instead shows `Unavailable:` with non-action `tgbtn:capacity`, whose toast explains removal by the control limit rather than claiming elapsed TTL. Both statuses consume no callback slot and store no prompt or retired-action registry. A missing original action or invalid publication address is unavailable, not evidence of a deadline; unknown history is never revived. Retirement diagnostics retain finite reason/count, action birth, configured store TTL, observed age and known publication coordinates; publication-unavailable/mismatch diagnostics do not spend a still-live action. Unrelated menu/SDK buttons, current history text and post-press feedback are preserved. Footer and canonical Rich-row snapshots are projected again immediately before native issuance after any queued predecessor; stale/unknown callback IDs cannot be restored by a late publication, and caller-owned snapshots are not mutated. Initial publication ACK after expiry may close the visible footer but cannot renew callbacks. Original-authority loss skips cleanup; an unknown edit invalidates the publication and its callback groups rather than authorizing a stale snapshot rewrite. Only a native method-bound rejection preserves the prior known snapshot/unspent IDs. Cleanup failures retire without replay. Store-resolved actions on managed publications carry only a bridge-local retirement marker: callback acknowledgement never re-edits a stale query keyboard after the publication owner has already taken visual cleanup. A delayed app result therefore cannot erase a newer independent collector footer or turn an uncertain cleanup into a second legacy attempt. Shutdown waits for actual publication work even if diagnostic stop fails; old shutdown continuations cannot act on successor state. Canonical in-body controls now retire through a guarded `editMessageText` using only the latest acknowledged plain-Markdown Rich snapshot and current footer, never a pre-edit body or an unknown outcome. Snapshot eligibility is at most 65,536 UTF-16 units with only `markdown`, `is_rtl` and `skip_entity_detection`; media, HTML/blocks and extra producer payloads are not cached/replayed for background cleanup. Original-authorized producer publications may still project their own Rich rows before issuance without transferring disclosure authority to cleanup. Canonical rows are opaque across multiline labels; fenced/inline/indented code and escaped markers remain literal. An acknowledged full-body replacement updates or clears the Rich cache and closes callback groups absent from the actual visible body/footer. Body and keyboard mutations share the same bounded native lane. This local source/mock/compiled evidence is not live client acceptance.

#### Separate SDK And Future Input Work

Companion extensions retain narrow Delivery functions, their private result/custody and exact transport/source authority. The private Text/Attachment foundations below remain unbound until their own privacy, source and resource guarantees are proved; they neither block ordinary agent selection markup nor authorize implicit model fallback. Future agent text/file formatting must explicitly define ordinary prompt/reply semantics rather than silently adopting SDK-private collectors. Artifact delivery and Task View remain separate SDK capabilities, not agent state-inspection commands. No production schema adoption, migration, new persistent root or general workflow engine is introduced.

Preserve direct/follower authority, sender admission, existing durable input/Queue ownership, `/new` exact source completion, `/compact` rechecks and hidden `/quit` shutdown ordering. Local parser/planner/callback fixtures are not current-session loading or live client acceptance. Remaining work belongs only in [BACKLOG.md](../BACKLOG.md#composable-interaction-surfaces-delivery).

#### Shared Input And Head/Tail Adoption (Approved, Partially Implemented)

The [adopted authoring/UX standard](./public-api.md#shared-input-and-question-lifetime-standard-adopted) changes the target from exact-reply-only SDK input to one positively owned next-text Input per operator/profile/bot/target, with recognized commands remaining commands and `/name` consuming the same primitive. New Input replaces its predecessor; Confirm/Choice replacement is not inferred. Existing Delivery question ownership is the common kernel, not a new dialog domain or interaction registry. Text result/semantic validation/rename effects remain producer-owned. Old associated answers and controls never borrow a successor's Input, even with identical target values.

The first checkpoint is implemented locally: optional SDK Input/Confirm/Choice `timeoutMs` defaults to 24 hours in `openQuestion()`, without changing explicit integer bounds, the admission-time deadline or required explicit Attachment timeout. Native boundary tests exercise the public Confirm/Choice membranes and private Text kernel; omission/short/invalid values, exact expiry and excluded Attachment behavior are covered, with a one-hour semantic falsifier restored by hash. That initial checkpoint did not change agent or `/name` lifetimes; production agent defaults are now 24 hours under the bounded direct composition below, while `/name` remains five minutes. Target-confined replacement is now implemented in the private kernel below. Remaining checkpoints are positively owned modal next-text selection, the built-in Name adapter, and agent/SDK head-tail coordination. A former otherwise-live head gets one hour from demotion; terminal state, lost original authority and producer deadlines still veto use. No promotion/resurrection of historical tail and no tap/edit renewal. Preserve existing finite numeric validation, original admission-time deadline anchoring, Name validation/reset/correction policy, source actual-I/O drain and capacity until their specific owner changes are validated. Unspecified media/voice/edit handling stays at existing restrictions rather than expanding capture.

The legacy exact-reply foundation and v4 witnesses below are retained implementation evidence, not modal next-text readiness. A missing marker cannot authorize ordinary handling or select an active Input: next-text capture needs positive current original Input ownership before ordinary/foreign/model handling, and the physical source must retain that exact choice across replacement, await, ACK uncertainty and terminal disposition. The proposed head lifetime does not by itself explain observed early expiry; loaded build, completion/group retirement, capacity and owner/binding loss are distinct evidence questions. Root/public API, donor/Bus/private receiver IPC, persistent/wire changes, production adoption/readiness, reload/live and release gates remain explicit; this standard does not grant those activations.

Current Routing command-priority preparation is implemented without changing Commands or opening SDK publication: the existing Name collector captures its original dialog, then uses `Commands.parseTelegramCommand()` on the text before name validation/consumption. Built-ins, ordinary extension commands, prompt templates and unknown-command fallback keep their normal dispatcher paths. Repeat `/name` opens a fresh dialog; other commands do not silently terminate its wait. A bare `/` or a slash inside a name remains subject to ordinary name policy rather than an ad-hoc slash ban. Private/historical reply fences still precede this collector; the change grants no SDK-reply-to-command fallback. SDK modal capture, common Name migration and shared head/tail remain separate checkpoints; the current Name dialog still has its own five-minute lifetime.

#### SDK Head/Tail Kernel (Private Opt-In)

The Delivery kernel now has a constructor-captured package-private `questionHeadTail?: true` mode; omission preserves existing production SDK behavior, while other runtime values refuse construction. It is not wired through the production bridge/root. The separate private first-send agent port below now exercises one direction; default agent callback assembly remains unchanged. Within this mode, a valid admitted Input/Confirm/Choice is head for at most 24 hours from original admission. Captured, otherwise-live previous SDK questions in the same profile/operator/exact chat/Thread scope are capped at one hour from this demotion or their earlier effective deadline. Existing tails already have the stricter deadline and are neither rewritten nor rearmed. The existing question entries own the effective deadline; irreversible shortening needs no separate head marker, second registry, persisted lifetime record or new SDK result surface. Explicit timeout validation remains 1–2,147,483,647 ms; longer valid requests are accepted but the private head policy caps effective lifetime. Attachment, Task View, Artifact and system-menu lifetimes are excluded.

Admission reserves the successor and demotes only its captured predecessors before disposal/drain callbacks can reenter. Replaced Input is terminal, not a tail. Finishing a head never promotes history, and a later question cannot renew an existing tail. Final abort/authority/deadline and static/capacity rejection do not demote a valid head. Demotion is a valid-admission event, not a publication-receipt reconstruction or a rollback grant if the new publication later fails. Each question's original timer owner rearms against its shortened effective deadline and fences already-dequeued callbacks by generation. Native controls and SDK settlement consult that same deadline. Logical expiry still leaves original publication work/lane retained; it cannot release Text opening capacity before actual I/O drains.

Mirrored native tests cover every cross-kind SDK demotion except terminal Input-to-Input replacement, late first demotion, no historical promotion, short producer deadlines, the 24-hour head cap, scope isolation, Attachment exclusion, final-preflight/capacity refusal, stale timer callbacks, captured opt-in, reentrant newer heads and held publication I/O. These are controlled same-runtime SDK facts, not agent membership, cross-owner IPC, source completion/ACK or live acceptance. The private first-send join below reuses this native lifetime owner under original scope; the private reciprocal subscriber and wider membership must preserve fixed edits/taps without a parallel interaction registry. Root/default/public Text/readiness, modal collection, `/name` migration, source recovery and reload/live/release gates remain separate.

#### Original SDK Lifetime Owner (Private, Unwired)

`captureQuestionLifetimeOwner()` is a package-private kernel port available only under the captured `questionHeadTail: true` opt-in. Copied method references share the same spent state. #### Original SDK Lifetime Scope Matching (Private, No Admission)

Every opt-in lifetime owner now exposes an opaque frozen native `scope` token and `assertScope(peerScope)`. A real local child-process witness exposed a narrower current-writer race beneath the v5 activation gate. `createJournalStoreCore()` now preserves the strict non-destructive source preflight **before** the transaction helper may create anything, but rechecks that exact native physical/namespace observation **inside** the acquired family transaction before any operation can use it.
